rows.note: Use this as the all-purpose construction for an action or situation that keeps happening over time, including repeated knocking and long-lasting rumours.

example.english: The persistent knocking outside is keeping me awake.
example.traditional: 門外一直有人敲門，我瞓唔着。
example.jyutping: mun4 ngoi6 jat1 zik6 jau5 jan4 haau1 mun4 ngo5 fan3 m4 zoek6

rows.note: Use this for someone who keeps trying and does not give up, usually with a positive tone.

example.english: They are persistent and practise running every day, eventually finishing a marathon.
example.traditional: 佢好有毅力，日日練跑，終於跑完馬拉松。
example.jyutping: keoi5 hou2 jau5 ngai6 lik6 jat6 jat6 lin6 paau2 zung1 jyu1 paau2 jyun4 maa5 laai1 cung4

rows.note: Use this for someone who pesters or presses on stubbornly and will not let go, usually negatively; it can also describe persistently repetitive behaviour directed at someone.

example.english: They were rejected several times but remained persistent, calling every day.
example.traditional: 佢俾人拒絕咗幾次，仲死纏爛打咁日日打電話嚟。
example.jyutping: keoi5 bei2 jan4 keoi5 zyut6 zo2 gei2 ci3 zung6 sei2 cin4 laan6 daa2 gam3 jat6 jat6 daa2 din6 waa2 lai4
